root.claim: One deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, refuting the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in this model.
root.method: Build the multiplier bottom-up: first the two power-saving tape procedures, then a convolution over a polynomial ring made from them, then the Gaussian-resampling and Bluestein reductions, then assemble the algorithm and add up its costs.

motivation.text: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so savings are needed in both address movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.
We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving is a power of the logarithm, $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$: tiny, but it breaks the long-standing $n\log n$ barrier because it comes from beating the per-level cost of both address movement and butterflies.

quote.quote: There are at most sixteen swaps and eight rotations in $S_0$.

children.claim: The exceptional addresses are found by a rank-counter scan costing $O(A_{\rm rect}^3)$ per record, and each destination $q'=T_0(S_0^{-1}(q))$ is computed by reversing the eight modular additions and applying the XORs.

quote.quote:
To implement the correction, scan the stream with a record-rank counter.
All chunk names are back in their original positions. Dividing the
current rank through the fixed seven field lengths recovers the three
chunk values and their mixed-radix record strides. The strides exclude
the $R$ payload bits. All involved integers have $O(A_{\rm rect})$ bits, so
schoolbook arithmetic, descriptor copying, and resets take at most
$O(A_{\rm rect}^3)$ per record. Test membership in $\mathcal B$ and extract just
those records.

children.claim: Stable binary radix sorting of only the extracted records by distinct destination keys, then one reinsertion scan, implements $T_0$ everywhere.

quote.quote:
Hold the full stream untouched
while stable binary radix sorting scans only the extracted records and
keys, least significant key bit first. Since $T_0S_0^{-1}$ permutes
$\mathcal B$, these keys are distinct and are exactly the ranks of the
marked holes. One forward full-stream scan reinserts the sorted records.
This implements $T_0$ everywhere.

children.claim: The most significant selected position is handled by a direct two-bit XOR in $O(V)$; when $f=1$ this is the entire algorithm.

quote.quote:
Finally apply the two-bit XOR to $x_{j_{f-1}},y_{j_{f-1}}$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}, splitting those chunks at the
selected positions and collapsing the other intervals. Its descriptor
again has a fixed number of positive lengths, each at most $V$.
This costs $O(V)$ and supplies the omitted selected position. When
$f=1$, $S_0,T_0$ are identities, $\mathcal B$ is empty, and this last
step is the entire algorithm.

children.claim: The movement costs $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ and the repair adds terms bounded by $A_{\rm rect}^3/R$ and $80(f-1)2^{-K}A_{\rm rect}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R)$ after division by $V$, both $o(1)$ under the family bounds.

quote.quote:
The movement costs $O(V(L^\tau+1))$. A fixed number of full record scans
costs $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3+V)$, and the at most $A_{\rm rect}$ radix passes cost
$O(|\mathcal B|A_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$; skip them when the extracted bank is empty.
The initial descriptor has a fixed number of canonical integers of
$O(A_{\rm rect})$ bits, so its preparation is covered by $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3)$.
All counters, positioning, rewinds, and cleanup are included.
Equation~\eqref{eq:packed-bad-fraction} proves
\eqref{eq:packed-rectangle-time} on a fixed number of tapes.
After division by $V=MR$, its additional terms are bounded by
$A_{\rm rect}^3/R$ and
$80(f-1)2^{-K}A_{\rm rect}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R)$. Under the stated family bounds
the first tends to zero, and the second is
$O(p^2 2^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$. This proves the final assertion.

children.claim: To add row $h'$ to row $h$ use slot $h'$ as $x$, slot $h$ as $y$ and any third slot as $z$; the lemma performs all the XORs $x_{h,j}\leftarrow x_{h,j}\oplus x_{h',j}$ at once and restores the third slot.

quote.quote:
To add row $h'$ to row $h$, use slot $h'$ as $x$,
slot $h$ as $y$, and any third, distinct slot as $z$ in
Lemma~\ref{lem:packed-selected-bit-rectangle}.  The lemma performs
$x_{h,j}\leftarrow x_{h,j}\mathbin\oplus x_{h',j}$ for every $j$ in
one operation and restores the third slot, whatever its initial
address value.

children.claim: One internal node on $e=m^k$ chunks costs $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$ beyond its $s$ child calls, each child acting on volume $V/W$, with the rows supplied by padding and splitting the first chunks.
children.method: Charge the binary basis changes by the packed procedure, supply rows from the leading chunks, split rows into $W$ role streams, and handle the case of few chunks by individual kernels.

motivation.text: The network needs $W$ equal-shape role streams, which a row index supplies; the first chunks provide it.

children.claim: Individual $C$ kernels are applied by splitting at the selected bit, scanning aligned record pairs and merging, so $e$ kernels cost $O(Ve)$.

quote.quote:
Thus \(e\) individual kernels cost
\(O(Ve)\) on any stream with these complete ranges and record format.

children.claim: At an internal node the phase construction gives exactly $s$ calls, and the binary changes of basis, scalar gates, corrections and reassembly cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$.

quote.quote:
The phase construction supplies one recursive call on a slot for each
vector in an edge residual basis, hence exactly \(s\) calls in one
invocation of the network.  If the logical volume entering this node
is \(V\), binary changes of basis, their inverses, scalar gates,
endpoint corrections and reassembly of the physical banks cost
\[
 O\bigl(V((eK)^\tau+1)\bigr)
\]
at this node.

children.claim: If $D\le q_0$, only individual $C$ kernels are used, at cost $O(V\log d)$.

quote.quote: If \(D\le q_0\), use individual \(C\) kernels, at cost \(O(V\log d)\).

children.claim: Otherwise the first $q_0$ chunks, treated individually, serve as the row index of range $R_{\rm row}=2^{q_0K}\ge W^{k_0}$, padded with zero rows to a multiple of $W^{k_0}$ so that at depth $j$ the row count is divisible by $W^{k_0-j}$.

quote.quote:
regard their concatenated bits as one row index.  Its range has
length \(R_{\rm row}=2^{q_0K}\ge W^{k_0}\), since \(K\ge1\) for sufficiently
large \(p\) and \(q_0K\ge k_0\log_2W\).  Within each preceding prefix, add
the same number of zero rows to reach the next multiple of \(W^{k_0}\);
the volume grows
by a factor at most two.  At any recursive depth \(j\le k_0\), the
row count is divisible by \(W^{k_0-j}\).

children.claim: A row index $u=Wg+w$ sends the whole row to role $w$, so each recursive edge call acts on one role stream of exactly $1/W$ of its parent's volume.

quote.quote:
At a node, write a row index as \(u=Wg+w\), with \(0\le w<W\),
and send that entire row to physical wire role \(w\), indexed there
by \(g\).  Every role stream has the same remaining address shape.
Thus a pointwise gate reads the records with the same \(g\) and the
same remaining address in its touched roles.  The scalar network
allows these role values to be arbitrary, so the split supplies its
scratch roles from existing rows.  Each recursive edge call acts on
one role stream with volume exactly \(1/W\) of its parent's logical
volume.

children.claim: Padded zero rows are again zero when an invocation finishes, so the added rows can be deleted afterwards.

quote.quote:
Each padded zero row is again zero when an invocation finishes, so the
added rows can be deleted after the invocations on the remaining chunks
have completed.

children.claim: With $F(e)$ the time divided by stream volume, $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$ for $e\ge d^\beta$ and $F(e)=O(e)$ below, which sums to $O(d^{\lambda'})$ over the base-$m$ pieces for any fixed $\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Unroll the recurrence: the per-node overhead is $O(e^\lambda)$ because $K\le e^{c/\beta}$, the internal levels form a geometric sum, the leaves stop at $e<d^\beta$, and the base-$m$ partition adds a logarithmic factor absorbed by $\lambda'$.

motivation.text: Stopping the recursion at $e<d^\beta$ turns the large chunk-width $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ into a mere power of $e$, so the overhead stays polynomially below linear.

children.salient: The leaves contribute $d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}$, which is why the exponent $\lambda'$ must exceed $\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)$ and recursion is stopped at $e=d^\beta$.

children.claim: Fix $\beta=1/2$ and exponents with $0<\tau<1$, $\max\{0,\log_m(s/W)\}\le\sigma<1$, $\max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1$ and $\tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda$.

quote.quote:
Fix \(\beta=1/2\), and choose real exponents satisfying
\[
 0<\tau<1,\qquad
 \max\{0,\log_m(s/W)\}\le\sigma<1,
 \qquad \max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1,
 \qquad \tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda.

children.claim: Recursion stops when $e<d^\beta$, and then $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$, $F(e)=O(e)$ for $e<d^\beta$.

quote.quote:
Stop recursion when
\(e<d^\beta\) and apply the \(e\) \(C\) kernels individually.  If
\(F(e)\) denotes time divided by the current logical stream volume,
then
\[
 F(e)\le (s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1),
 \qquad F(e)=O(e)\quad(e<d^\beta).

children.claim: The $s$ child calls run on streams of volume $V/W$, costing $s(V/W)F(e/m)$, so dividing by $V$ gives the factor $s/W$.

quote.quote:
Indeed, the \(s\) child calls are executed on streams of volume
\(V/W\), so their total cost is \(s(V/W)F(e/m)\).  Dividing by
the current volume \(V\) gives the factor \(s/W\).

children.claim: At an internal node $e\ge d^\beta$ gives $K\le d^c\le e^{c/\beta}$, so the overhead is $O(e^{\tau(1+c/\beta)}+1)=O(e^\lambda)$.

quote.quote:
At an internal node \(e\ge d^\beta\), hence
\(K\le d^c\le e^{c/\beta}\).  The overhead is therefore
\(O(e^{\tau(1+c/\beta)}+1)=O(e^\lambda)\).

children.claim: With $a=s/W\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda$ the internal costs sum to at most $Ce^\lambda\sum_{j\ge0}(a/m^\lambda)^j=O(e^\lambda)$.

quote.quote:
Put \(a=s/W\).  Since \(a\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda\), the internal
costs sum to at most
\[
 C e^\lambda\sum_{j\ge0}(a/m^\lambda)^j=O(e^\lambda).

children.claim: The leaves after $j$ levels, each with $u=e/m^j<d^\beta$ chunks, contribute at most $O(a^ju)\le O(e^\sigma u^{1-\sigma})\le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)})$, using $a^j\le m^{j\sigma}=(e/u)^\sigma$.

quote.quote:
If the leaves after \(j\) levels contain \(u=e/m^j<d^\beta\)
active chunks each, their combined normalized
contribution is at most
\[
 O(a^ju)\le O(e^\sigma u^{1-\sigma})
          \le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)}).
\]
The first inequality uses
\(a^j\le m^{j\sigma}=(e/u)^\sigma\).

children.claim: Splitting $D-q_0=\sum_ja_jm^j$ in base $m$ into at most $(m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_md\rfloor)$ pieces gives $O(\log(2d)[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}+1])=O(d^{\lambda'})$ for any fixed $\max\{\lambda,\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)\}<\lambda'<1$.

quote.quote:
Write \(D-q_0=\sum_j a_jm^j\) in base \(m\), with \(0\le a_j<m\).
Partition the remaining chunks into \(a_j\) consecutive pieces
containing \(m^j\) chunks for each \(j\).
There are at most \((m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_m d\rfloor)\) pieces.
Adding their costs and the row preprocessing gives
\[
 O\!\left(\log(2d)
    \bigl[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}+1\bigr]\right)
   =O(d^{\lambda'})
\]
for any fixed
\[
 \max\{\lambda,\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)\}<\lambda'<1.

children.claim: The whole layer can be evaluated exactly with $p+\Delta$ fractional bits and $\Delta+3$ integer bits per real component, where $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil=o(p)$.
children.method: Bound the arithmetic dependency depth $A(e)$ along any chain by the recurrence $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$, then convert depth into denominator and magnitude growth.

motivation.text: Each addition can double the modulus and each halving adds a denominator bit, so the number of operations on a chain bounds both growths.

children.claim: Put $E=64(W+m+1)^3$, $B=s+E$, $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\}$, $C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\}$, $C_0=128mB^2$ and $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$.

quote.quote:
E=64(W+m+1)^3,\qquad B=s+E,
 \qquad \nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},
\]
and set
\[
 C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\},\qquad C_0=128mB^2,
 \qquad \Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil.

children.claim: Every physical wire occurs in at most twelve scalar gates, there are at most $12W$ gates, and evaluating all outputs of a gate takes at most $2W^2$ elementary operations.

quote.quote:
The scalar schedule \eqref{eq:motif-schedule} touches a data wire
at most four times in each of the three stages.  A scratch wire belongs
to one invocation and is touched at most four times there.  Thus every
physical wire occurs in at most twelve scalar gates, and there are
at most \(12W\) gates.  A gate has at most \(W\) inputs and outputs
and coefficients in \(\{0,\pm1,\pm1/2\}\).  One output is a sum of
at most \(W\) terms, each requiring at most one halving and one
addition or subtraction.  Evaluating all outputs from saved inputs
therefore takes at most \(2W^2\) elementary operations.

children.claim: The child corrections take at most $4s$ operations and the endpoint corrections $4W+4$, and since $s<Wm$ the total $24W^3+4s+4W+4$ is less than $E$.

quote.quote:
This gives at most \(4s\) operations for the child corrections.
The source, sink and bank corrections take at most \(4W+4\) more.
Calculating the address parities and phase exponents is address or descriptor
work, not arithmetic on coefficients.  Since \(s<Wm\), the total
\(24W^3+4s+4W+4\) is less than
\(E=64(W+m+1)^3\).

children.claim: A paired kernel evaluation uses at most eight operations, so $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$ at an internal node and $A(e)\le8e$ at a leaf; depth concatenates all $s$ calls and so uses $s$, not $s/W$.

quote.quote:
We may therefore use
\[
 A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E
 \quad\hbox{at an internal node},\qquad A(e)\le8e
 \quad\hbox{at a leaf}.
\]
The depth estimate concatenates the \(s\) calls, so it uses \(s\).
The factor \(1/W\) in the earlier time recurrence accounted for
their smaller stream volumes.

children.claim: For $x\ge1$, $sx+E\le(s+E)x=Bx$; with at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels and $B^{k+1}\le B^2d^{\log_mB}\le B^2d^\nu$ this gives $A(e)\le8dB^{k+1}\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}$.

quote.quote:
There are at most \(k\le\lceil\log_m d\rceil\) internal levels.
For any bound \(x\ge1\), \(sx+E\le(s+E)x=Bx\).
Starting with \(8e\le8d\le8dB\) at a leaf and applying this
inequality through the levels gives the first bound below.
For the second, use \(B\le m^\nu\) and
\[
 B^{k+1}\le B^{\log_m d+2}
          =B^2d^{\log_m B}\le B^2d^\nu.
\]
Thus
\[
 A(e)\le 8dB^{k+1}\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}.

children.claim: Concatenating the at most $md$ base-$m$ pieces adds depth $8mB^2d^{\nu+2}$, and at most $d$ individual kernels add $8d$.

quote.quote:
For the sufficiently large sizes under consideration, the earlier
piece count is at most \(md\).  Concatenating their depths contributes
at most \(8mB^2d^{\nu+2}\).  In either preprocessing branch, at most
\(d\) individual kernels are used, contributing at most \(8d\).

children.claim: A value at depth $\ell$ lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ and has modulus at most $2^\ell$: addition at most doubles the modulus, halving adds one denominator bit, and signs and multiplication by $i$ preserve both.

quote.quote:
A value at depth \(\ell\)
lies in \(2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]\) and has modulus at most
\(2^\ell\).  This follows by induction: addition or subtraction
can at most double the maximum modulus of its operands; halving adds
at most one denominator bit; and signs and multiplication by \(i\)
preserve both bounds.

children.claim: Reserving $p+\Delta$ fractional bits and $\Delta+3$ integer and sign bits per real component therefore represents every intermediate coefficient exactly.

quote.quote:
Thus reserving \(p+\Delta\)
fractional bits and \(\Delta+3\) integer and sign bits per real
component represents every intermediate coefficient exactly and
prevents overflow.

children.claim: Choosing $\epsilon C_1<1$ with $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$ gives $\Delta=o(p)$, so the full coefficient width is $O(p)$.

quote.quote:
Choose \(\epsilon C_1<1\).  Since \(d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)\),
\(\Delta=o(p)\), and the full coefficient width is \(O(p)\), as
required in the time analysis.

children.claim: The extra normalized terms of the packed lemma tend to zero uniformly over the allowed $d,r$, so every packed call has cost $O(M_{\rm child}R_{\rm g}(L^\tau+1))$ with one common constant.

quote.quote:
Both bounds tend to zero uniformly over all current allowed $d,r$.
Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:packed-selected-bit-rectangle} has the required
$O(M_{\rm child}R_{\rm g}(L^\tau+1))$ cost for every packed call,
with one common time constant.

children.claim: The row construction and the recurrence analysis give total time $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ on fixed tapes, including padded and auxiliary streams, and the layer identity converts the exact $C$-layer to $\mathcal H$.

quote.quote:
The row construction and the recurrence analysis
above give total time $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ on fixed tapes, including
all padded and auxiliary streams. Equation~\eqref{eq:phase-butterfly-layer}
converts the resulting exact $C$-layer to $\mathcal H$.

children.claim: Every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one, so $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and componentwise truncation keeps the disk and errs by less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote:
Finally, every row of $\mathcal H$ has
absolute row sum one. Thus $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk
arrays, and componentwise truncation preserves that disk and has
error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$: truncation cannot increase the
absolute value of either component, and changes each by less than
$2^{-p}$.

children.claim: Two forward synthetic transforms in layout order, a pointwise ring product divided by $r$, the opposite transform and an exact scaling by $M$ compute the normalized convolution $\mathcal M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T$ over $\mathcal R_r$ with error below $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$ and cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}+\log(rp)])$.
children.method: Build it from the transform with retained frequency order, the layout that makes every round a simultaneous layer, and the signed-packing ring product; then verify normalization and add errors.

motivation.text: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation to both operands, so the forward outputs can be multiplied in their retained order and passed directly to the opposite procedure.

quote.quote:
Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record
permutation $LB$ to both operands.  We may therefore multiply the
forward outputs in their retained order and pass that order directly
to the opposite procedure.

adds.name: axis bits
adds.meaning: the base-2 logarithm of the polynomial length, $\ell=\log_2r$, which is the number of address bits of a long axis

adds.name: record count
adds.meaning: the number of polynomial records, $M=T/r$, one for each point of the first $d-1$ axes

children.claim: On $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ the transforms $F_t^\pm$ with roots $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$ are contractions with $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$, and $F_t^-$ is computed by decimation-in-frequency rounds of $H_0$ butterflies and monomial twiddles.
children.method: Treat powers of $y$ as roots of unity acting by signed shifts, prove character cancellation directly, and split each transform into pairs $z_k,z_{k+t/2}$ so that the length-$t/2$ procedure recurses on each branch.

motivation.text: The ring has zero divisors, so character cancellation is verified directly instead of dividing by $\omega_t^j-1$.

quote.quote:
The ring has zero divisors, so we verify character cancellation
directly instead of dividing by $\omega_t^j-1$.

adds.name: transform length
adds.meaning: the length of the transform, a power of two dividing $2r$

adds.name: synthetic root
adds.meaning: the power $y^{2r/t}$ of the ring variable, acting as a primitive $t$-th root of unity by a signed shift

children.claim: Every power of $\omega_t$ is an isometry and each transform entry averages $t$ such images, so both transforms are contractions.

quote.quote:
Every power of $\omega_t$ is an isometry, and each transform entry is
an average of $t$ such images.  Thus both transforms are contractions.

children.claim: $\sum_{k=0}^{t-1}\omega_t^{jk}$ equals $t$ if $t\mid j$ and $0$ otherwise, hence $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$.
children.method: Pair the summands by a shift $k\mapsto k+t/2^{v+1}$ that multiplies the sum by $y^{rj_0}=-1$, then expand the composite transforms.

motivation.text: Because $\mathcal R_r$ has zero divisors the usual geometric-series argument is unavailable, but a sign-changing shift of the index works.

children.salient: Character cancellation holds in a ring with zero divisors, because $y^{rj_0}=-1$ makes the shifted sum equal to its own negative.

children.claim: Writing $j=2^vj_0$ with $j_0$ odd, replacing $k$ by $k+t/2^{v+1}$ modulo $t$ permutes the summands and multiplies their sum by $y^{rj_0}=-1$, so the sum vanishes because the additive group has no two-torsion.

quote.quote:
Write $j=2^v j_0$ with $j_0$ odd
and $0\leq v<\log_2t$.  Replacing $k$ by $k+t/2^{v+1}$ modulo $t$ permutes
the summands and multiplies their sum by
$y^{rj_0}=-1$.  Hence the sum is zero, since the additive group of
$\mathcal R_r$ has no two-torsion.

children.claim: Expanding the composite transforms and using this identity proves $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$.

quote.quote:
Expanding the composite transforms
and applying this identity proves the final formula.

children.claim: The decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$, applies $H_0$, multiplies the $b=1$ output by $\omega_t^{-k}$ and recurses on each branch, computing $F_t^-$ by $(F_t^-z)_{2h+b}=\frac{1}{t/2}\sum_k(\omega_t^2)^{-hk}\omega_t^{-bk}\frac{z_k+(-1)^bz_{k+t/2}}2$.
The recursion writes frequency $j$ in slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$, and the opposite procedure consuming that order implements $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$, so no sort is executed.
children.method: Track which address-bit slots hold frequency bits after each level, then traverse the recursion in reverse for the opposite transform and count its scale factors.

motivation.text: The recursion writes its outputs directly in this order and does not move whole frequency indices.

quote.quote: directly in this order; it does not move whole frequency indices.

children.salient: The bit-reversal permutation $B_t$ is never executed: it stays inside the stored order, and the opposite transform undoes it by running the recursion backwards.

children.claim: After $s$ levels the values of the first $s$ named slots are branch bits, identified as frequency bits $0,\dots,s-1$ from the least significant end.

quote.quote:
For $0\leq s\leq a$, after $s$ levels the values of
the first $s$ named slots are branch bits $b_0,\ldots,b_{s-1}$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:synthetic-dif} identifies these as frequency bits
$0,\ldots,s-1$, numbered from the least significant bit.

children.claim: After all $a$ rounds the slots from high to low hold the frequency bits from low to high, so $(F_t^-z)_j$ occupies slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$; call this record permutation $B_t$.

quote.quote:
After all $a$ rounds, the named slots from high to low therefore
contain the frequency bits from low to high.  If
$\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$ reverses the $a$ binary digits of $j$, the
entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ occupies slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$.

children.claim: Since $H_0^2=I/2$ each reversed level is half the inverse of its forward level, and with $a=\log_2t$ levels the reverse procedure composed with $B_tF_t^-$ is $2^{-a}I=I/t$.

quote.quote:
As $H_0^2=I/2$, the reversed level is half the inverse
of the corresponding forward level.  There are $a=\log_2t$ levels,
so the reverse procedure composed with $B_tF_t^-$ is
$2^{-a}I=I/t$.

children.claim: Character cancellation gives the same composite for $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$, so the two reverse operators agree and the exact procedures implement $B_tF_t^-$ and $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$.

A layout permutation $L$ places the selected bits of all axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks, so every round is one simultaneous layer, and the forward and opposite procedures cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$ with error below $\sqrt2\,\ell\,2^{-p}$.
children.method: Move one slot of each long axis and the lowest slots to a prefix, exchange width-$K$ chunks so the remaining slots sit chunk by chunk, run each round on the layout with one truncation, and add per-round errors.

motivation.text: To apply the simultaneous layer in a round, the selected bits of the participating axes must sit at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

quote.quote:
To apply Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} in a transform round,
we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common
offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

children.salient: The cost has three terms of different character: the prefix moves $dK$ and the chunk exchanges $pK^{\tau-1}$ both depend on the chunk width $K$ in opposite ways, which forces $K$ to grow, but only slowly.

children.claim: A round applies one $H_0$ per participating axis, and the twiddle of one axis commutes with the other axes' butterflies, so a round is a parallel butterfly followed by one recordwise monomial $J_E$.

quote.quote:
A round applies one current $H_0$ on each participating axis.  The
twiddle for axis $i$ depends only on that axis's address bits.
The two entries paired by another axis's butterfly have the same
axis-$i$ address, so that twiddle commutes with the other butterfly.
Consequently the individual axis steps may be grouped as a parallel
butterfly $\mathcal H$, followed by one recordwise monomial operation
$J_E$.

children.claim: The at most $D(b+1)=O(dK)$ listed slots moved to a prefix cost $O(TpdK)$.

quote.quote:
Form a list of the slots to move to a prefix.  First list
$(i,\ell-1)$ for the length-$2^\ell$ axes in increasing $i$.
Then list $(i,h)$ for $h=b-1,\ldots,0$, and within each $h$ in
increasing $i$; this second list is empty if $b=0$.  Move each listed
slot immediately after the prefix already formed, leaving all other
slots in their relative order.  There are at most $D(b+1)=O(dK)$
listed slots, so the moves cost $O(TpdK)$.

children.claim: Step 1: apply the address map $\Phi$ with its padded layout to obtain source arrays $u,v$ of exact $p$-bit grid values of norm below $1/4$.

quote.quote:
Apply the coefficient-address map $\Phi$, with its padded layout, to obtain
source arrays $u,v$.  Their coefficients are exact $p$-bit grid
values of norm less than $1/4$.

children.claim: Step 2: compute the two source transforms $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(u)$ and $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(v)$.

quote.quote:
Compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(u)$ and
$\widetilde{\mathscr F}(v)$.

children.claim: Step 3: multiply corresponding coefficients exactly and truncate each part toward zero to $p$ fractional bits, giving the source array $z$.

quote.quote:
Multiply corresponding complex coefficients exactly and truncate
each real and imaginary part toward zero to $p$ fractional bits, writing
the result in the common $w_{\rm c}$-bit component format.
Denote the resulting source array by $z$.

children.claim: Step 4: compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^+(z)$ and multiply its numerators exactly by $S$, giving the dyadic array $\widetilde w$.

quote.quote:
Compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)$ and multiply its grid
numerators exactly by $S$, retaining the denominator $2^p$ and writing
each component in signed width $w_{\rm c}+b$. Denote the represented
dyadic array by $\widetilde w$.

children.claim: Step 5: multiply by $2^{2b+4}S$, round the real values to nearest integers as signed $(3b+1)$-bit words (zero at padded addresses), and apply $\Phi^{-1}$ to restore coefficient order.

quote.quote:
Multiply the grid numerators of $\widetilde w$ exactly by
$2^{2b+4}S$, again retaining the denominator $2^p$, and write each
component in signed width $w_{\rm c}+4b+4$. Round the represented real
values to the nearest integers. At each valid address, write the rounded
coefficient in one signed $(3b+1)$-bit word, most significant bit first;
at every padded address,
write a zero word of that width. Supply this local payload width to
$\Phi^{-1}$ and apply it, including removal of the address padding, to
restore the ordinary coefficient order.

children.claim: The two occurrences of $S$ undo different normalisations: after the three transforms the exact result is $(u*v)/S^2$, the first scale gives $w=(u*v)/S$ and the second, with $2^{2b+4}$, gives the original integer coefficient convolution.

quote.quote:
The two occurrences of $S$ in this algorithm undo different
normalizations.  By \eqref{eq:source-permutation-cancel}, the exact
counterpart after the three transforms is $(u*v)/S^2$, so after the
first scale it is $w=(u*v)/S$.  The second scale gives
$2^{2b+4}(u*v)$, whose inverse image under $\Phi$ is the original
integer coefficient convolution.

children.claim: With $h_p=2^{-p}$ and $L=\log_2T$, the scale bookkeeping and the error chain show that every recovered coefficient has error below $448\,b\,2^{-b+\gamma}<\tfrac12$, so it rounds to the true integer, which is below $2^{3b}$.
children.method: Propagate norms and errors through each stage in the max-modulus norm using that a linear contraction does not enlarge an input error and a bilinear contraction adds the two operand errors, then undo the scales and compare with $1/2$.

motivation.text: A linear contraction propagates an input error without increasing it, and for a bilinear contraction on disk operands the two errors add.

quote.quote:
A linear contraction propagates an input error without increasing it.
For a bilinear contraction $\mathcal M$, replacing its operands gives
\[
 \|\mathcal M(f',g')-\mathcal M(f,g)\|
 \le \|f'-f\|\,\|g'\|+\|f\|\,\|g'-g\|.
\]
When all four operands are in the disk, their two errors therefore add.

children.salient: Despite scales up to $2^\gamma S T^2$ and $2^{2b+4}$, the final error $448\,b\,2^{-b+\gamma}$ still falls like $2^{-b}$, because the working precision $6b$ outweighs the rescaling.

the three transform errors and the polynomial-product truncation total
less than $3L+2$.  Thus the error of the returned normalized
convolution is bounded by

 E_{\rm ring}:=M(3L+2)<5TL.

children.claim: If one operand has norm at most $.7$, bilinear contraction keeps the computed output below $.7+5TLh_p<.701$ without clipping.

quote.quote:
If one operand has norm at most $.7$, bilinear contraction gives
$\|\mathcal M_r(f,g)\|\le.7$.  Its computed grid output consequently
has norm less than $.7+5TLh_p<.701$ for large $n$.

children.claim: The two input twists (each below $4h_p$), the convolution ($E_{\rm ring}$) and the output untwist (below $4h_p$) give $\|\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}-\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}\|<6TLh_p$.

quote.quote:
Its bilinear contraction bound propagates the two input twist errors,
each less than $4$.  Its approximation contributes $E_{\rm ring}$,
and the output untwist contributes less than $4$.  All these
comparisons are at the normalized $\mathcal M_r$ interface, after its
factor $M$.  They give
\[
 \|\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(f,g)
            -\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)\|
 <(E_{\rm ring}+4+4+4)h_p<6TLh_p.

children.claim: Adding the kernel approximation (2), first phase (4), convolution ($6TL$) and last phase (4) gives $\|\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)-QF_{\boldsymbol t}x\|<8TLh_p$.

quote.quote:
The computed convolution contributes less
than $6TL$, and the last endpoint multiplication less than $4$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:permuted-chirp} identifies the exact result, so
\[
 \|\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)-QF_{\boldsymbol t}x\|
 <(6TL+2+4+4)h_p<8TLh_p.

children.claim: Inserting the exact contractions $\mathcal A,QF_{\boldsymbol t},\mathcal B_0$, the error before the source scale is below $2dp^2+8TL$, and after the scale $2^\gamma$ it is below $E_sh_p$ with $E_s=9\,2^\gamma TL$.

quote.quote:
Insert the exact contractions $\mathcal A$, $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$,
and $\mathcal B_0$ at the computed inputs.  The error before the
source scale is less than $2dp^2+8TL$.  Multiplication by
$2^\gamma$ therefore gives error less than
$2^\gamma(2dp^2+8TL)h_p$, which is bounded by $E_sh_p$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:source-error}
 E_s=9\,2^\gamma TL,
\end{equation}
because $2dp^2<TL$ eventually.

children.claim: The computed transforms have norm below $1/4+E_sh_p<.26$, so $z=Q_p(\widetilde U\cdot\widetilde V_1)$ has norm at most $.26^2<.5$.

quote.quote:
The exact arrays have norm less than $1/4$, and the computed arrays
have norm less than $1/4+E_sh_p<.26$.  Hence
$z=Q_p(\widetilde U\cdot\widetilde V_1)$ has norm at most
$.26^2<.5$.

children.claim: Splitting $\widetilde U\widetilde V_1-UV_1$ into two terms each below $E_sh_p$ and adding truncation $2h_p$ gives $\|z-U\cdot V_1\|<(2E_s+2)h_p$.

quote.quote:
The factors $\widetilde V_1$ and $U$ are in the disk.  The two terms
have total norm less than $2E_sh_p$, and truncation adds less than $2h_p$.
Thus $\|z-U\cdot V_1\|<(2E_s+2)h_p$.

children.claim: Since $G(U\cdot V_1)=(u*v)/S^2$ for the exact opposite contraction $G=RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}$, inserting $G$ at the computed input gives $\|\widetilde{\mathscr F}^+(z)-G(U\cdot V_1)\|<(3E_s+2)h_p$.

quote.quote:
The computed opposite transform may be applied to $z$ because
$\|z\|<.5$. Insert $G$ at that computed input:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)-G(U\cdot V_1)\|
 &\le \|\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)-Gz\|\\
 &\qquad+\|G(z-U\cdot V_1)\|\\
 &<(3E_s+2)h_p.

children.claim: The first scale by $S$ gives $\widetilde w$ approximating $w=(u*v)/S$ with error below $E_wh_p$, where $E_w:=S(3E_s+2)<28\,2^\gamma T^2L$.

quote.quote:
The first exact numerator multiplication by $S$ gives
$\widetilde w$, approximating $w=(u*v)/S$ with error less than
$E_wh_p$, where
\[
 E_w:=S(3E_s+2)<28\,2^\gamma T^2L.

children.claim: Each coefficient of $w$ averages $S$ products of coefficients of $u$ and $v$, so $\|w\|<1/16$ and $\|\widetilde w\|<1/16+E_wh_p<1$.

quote.quote:
Each coefficient of $w$ is an average of $S$ products of coefficients
of $u$ and $v$, so $\|w\|<1/16$.  The earlier cutoff therefore gives
\[
 \|\widetilde w\|<1/16+E_wh_p<1/16+10^{-3}<1.

children.claim: The second scale by $2^{2b+4}S$ returns the integer coefficients, and since $S\le T<2^b$, $L<b$, $\gamma\le b/4$, the final error is below $2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\,2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b}<448b\,2^{-b+\gamma}\le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<\tfrac12$.
The true coefficients are integers, so an error strictly below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to $H_j/2^p$ the unique correct coefficient.

quote.quote:
The true coefficients are real integers.  If $H_j$ is the real
numerator after the second scaling, its represented value is
$H_j/2^p$.  The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to
that value the unique correct coefficient.

children.claim: By the capacity bound the correct coefficient lies in $[0,2^{3b})$ and fits in one signed $(3b+1)$-bit word.

quote.quote:
bound makes the result the correct nonnegative coefficient, and

children.claim: Radix-$2^b$ carry propagation turns the recovered coefficients $c_j<2^{3b}$ into exactly $2n$ product bits.
children.method: Run the carry recurrence $c_j+k_j=d_j+Q_0k_{j+1}$ from low to high index, bound the carries by induction, and check the digit invariant.

motivation.text: The coefficients may exceed one digit, but the carry stays bounded, so a left-to-right scan with $O(b)$-bit carry suffices.

children.claim: With $Q_0=2^b$ the carries obey $k_0=0$, $d_j=(c_j+k_j)\bmod Q_0$, $k_{j+1}=\lfloor(c_j+k_j)/Q_0\rfloor$, and the coefficients are zero for $2q-2<j<S$.

quote.quote:
To propagate carries, let $Q_0=2^b$.  The recovered ordinary
coefficients are the $c_j$ in \eqref{eq:capacity}; they are zero for
$2q-2<j<S$.  With $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ as
above, use the recurrence for $0\le j<S$:
\[
 k_0=0,\qquad d_j=(c_j+k_j)\bmod Q_0,\qquad
 k_{j+1}=\left\lfloor\frac{c_j+k_j}{Q_0}\right\rfloor.

children.claim: The carries satisfy $0\le k_j\le q(Q_0-1)<Q_0^2$: if this holds at $j$ then $c_j+k_j\le q(Q_0-1)^2+q(Q_0-1)=qQ_0(Q_0-1)$, which proves the bound at $j+1$.

quote.quote:
The carries satisfy $0\le k_j\le q(Q_0-1)<Q_0^2$.  If this holds at
$j$, then
\[
 c_j+k_j\le q(Q_0-1)^2+q(Q_0-1)=qQ_0(Q_0-1),
\]
which proves the next carry bound.

children.claim: The defining relation gives the invariant $\sum_{h<j}c_hQ_0^h=\sum_{h<j}d_hQ_0^h+k_jQ_0^j$, which fixes the first $j$ radix digits of the full product.

quote.quote:
The defining relation
$c_j+k_j=d_j+Q_0k_{j+1}$ also gives the exact invariant
\[
 \sum_{h<j}c_hQ_0^h
   =\sum_{h<j}d_hQ_0^h+k_jQ_0^j.
\]
It holds for $j=0$, and the defining relation proves its next instance.
The unprocessed terms are multiples of $Q_0^j$, so the identity fixes
the first $j$ radix digits of the full product.

children.claim: The exact product is below $2^{2n}$, so all bits above position $2n-1$ are zero; removing only those padding bits yields exactly $2n$ output bits.

quote.quote:
than $2^{2n}$; all bits above position $2n-1$ are therefore zero.
Remove only those zero padding bits and retain leading zeros as needed
to produce exactly $2n$ bits.

children.claim: Dividing the costs by $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ gives seven dominant terms (butterfly rounds, chunk exchanges, simultaneous layers, CRT layouts, Gaussian lines, chirps, packed products), each at most $p^{1-2\kappa}$, so the total is $O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$.

motivation.text: The explicit slack between the smallest margin $2^{-181}$ and $\kappa=2^{-182}$ will cover any remaining fixed power of $\log p$.

quote.quote:
This explicit slack will cover
any remaining fixed power of $\log p$.

children.salient: The smallest margin $2^{-181}$ comes from the chunk-exchange term, $\epsilon c(1-\tau)=2^{-75}\cdot2^{-56}\cdot2^{-50}$, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is exactly half of it, which pays for every logarithmic factor.

children.claim: Put $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$; each coefficient has $\Theta(p)$ bits, so a full padded array has $\Theta(V)$ stored bits.

quote.quote:
For the cost calculation put $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$. The fixed-width coefficient
formats use $\Theta(p)$ bits per coefficient, so a full padded array has
$\Theta(V)$ stored bits.

g_1&=1-\epsilon(1+c),\qquad
 g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau),\qquad
 g_3=\epsilon(1-\lambda'),\\

children.claim: The transform layout uses $O(p/K)$ exchanges of width-$K$ chunks, each costing $O(VK^\tau)$, so the normalized total is $O(p/K)K^\tau=O(pK^{\tau-1})$, a power $1-\epsilon c(1-\tau)$ of $p$.

quote.quote:
Its positional layout uses $O(p/K)$ exchanges
of width-$K$ chunks, because $d\ell=O(p)$. Each exchange costs
$O(VK^\tau)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:chunk-swap}, so the normalized total is
\[
 O(p/K)\,K^\tau=O(pK^{\tau-1}).

children.claim: The at most $\ell$ simultaneous rounds each cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, already including basis changes, repair, row padding and cleanup.

quote.quote:
For the at most $\ell$ simultaneous rounds,
Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} supplies $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$
per round. Its bound already includes the binary basis changes,
deterministic repair, row padding and removal, all base-$m$ groups,
and fixed-tape cleanup.

children.claim: Axis exposure and restoration need $O(d^2)$ adjacent axis moves, each costing $O(V(1+\ell^\tau))$ by peeling the excess bit, exchanging equal-width parts and restoring the bit.

quote.quote:
Axis exposure and restoration require $O(d^2)$ adjacent axis moves.
Each costs $O(V(1+\ell^\tau))$: peel a single excess bit when widths
differ by one, exchange their equal-width parts, and restore the bit.

children.claim: Axis $i$ has at most $T/t_i$ Gaussian lines, so the line costs sum to $O(dTp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ and, with $\alpha=\Theta(p^{1/4+\epsilon/2})$, the normalized power is $3/4+\delta+3\epsilon/2$.

quote.quote:
For Gaussian resampling, axis $i$ has at most $T/t_i$ processed lines.
The line-machine costs therefore sum to
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^d\frac{T}{t_i}
       O(t_i p^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)
 =O(dTp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha).
\]
Dividing by $V=Tp$ gives the fifth row.  The factor
$\alpha=\Theta(p^{1/4+\epsilon/2})$ explains its displayed power of $p$.

children.claim: Chirp numerators are computed with the established multiplier and the exponentials generated at cost $O(dp^{1+\delta})$ per entry.

quote.quote: then generating the exponentials, costs $O(dp^{1+\delta})$ per entry.

children.claim: There are $T/r$ polynomial records in each pointwise ring product, and four integer products on $O(rp)$ bits per record cost $O(Tp\log(rp))$ in total.

quote.quote:
polynomial records in each pointwise ring product.  Four integer
products on $O(rp)$ bits per record therefore cost
$O(Tp\log(rp))$ in total.

children.claim: These calls use the established multiplier on records of length $O(rp)=o(n)$ and do not invoke the improved algorithm recursively.

quote.quote:
use the previously established multiplier on records of length
$O(rp)=o(n)$; they do not call the improved algorithm being constructed.

children.claim: The recursion and layout visits number at most $p^A$ with setup $p^C$ each, so setup costs at most $p^{A+C}=o(Tp)$.

quote.quote:
Choose a fixed exponent $A$ so that their
total number of visits is at most $p^A$, and a fixed $C$ bounding
descriptor setup performed once per visit by $p^C$ steps.  This setup then
costs at most $p^{A+C}=o(Tp)$.

children.claim: The compact sorting of exceptional records totals $O(dp2^{-K}\sum V_{\rm call})=O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V)$ in the worst case.

quote.quote:
Stable bit sorting makes $O(p)$ scans of this stream, for one-call
cost $O(V_{\rm call}dp2^{-K})$.  Extraction and reinsertion use a
constant number of scans of the full current volume; those scans are
already in the node overhead.  Since there are at most $p^A$ visits,
each of volume $O(V)$, the compact sorting costs sum to at most
\[
 O\!\left(dp2^{-K}\sum_{\rm calls}V_{\rm call}\right)
   =O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V)

children.claim: Each of the seven powers is at most $1-2\kappa$ and any fixed power of $\log p$ is at most $p^\kappa$ eventually, so the total is $O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$.

quote.quote:
Each of the seven displayed powers is at most $1-2\kappa$ by
\eqref{eq:margin-list}.  Any fixed power of $\log p$ is at most $p^\kappa$
eventually.  The complete large-input bound is consequently
\[
 O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}).

children.claim: Below a fixed cutoff beyond all size, precision, margin and layout conditions schoolbook multiplication is used, and the finitely many smaller lengths are absorbed in the constant.

quote.quote:
Fix one cutoff beyond all the size, precision, margin and layout
conditions, and use schoolbook multiplication below it.  The finitely
many smaller lengths are included by enlarging the implicit constant.
